html:
SMTO-CMP-0026 — A required step in this task failed and wasn't fixed

GUID: 333f7515-fb17-4c5a-a77c-3dcc2e3a0866
Slug: completion-required-operation-unsuccessful
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • A step this task depends on failed, and nothing later fixed it. SMTO won't mark the task finished until that step works or the failure is clearly reported. Steps that worked are kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Expand the task, find the step marked Failed, and open it to read its output and error message. The message usually names the real cause, such as a missing file, a wrong path or missing access.
  2. If the error points to something you control, such as a missing file, password or permission, fix that first. The step will keep failing the same way until its cause is fixed.
  3. Check whether the failed step changed anything, for example whether the file or setting it touched was partly updated. A failed step can still make part of a change, and repeating it blindly could make that worse.
  4. Send a message asking SMTO to check the current state and redo only the failed step. SMTO looks again first and avoids repeating the steps that already worked.

What success looks like

  • The step now shows Completed and the task finishes as Completed.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them, with the failed step's error, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rerun the whole task; steps that worked would run again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Completion was rejected because a result marked required has a non-success status, is not an accepted complete read observation, and is not superseded by a later successful result.

What this means

  • A required operation remains non-successful and is neither an accepted complete observation nor superseded by a later successful reconciled result. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • A required operation remains non-successful and is neither an accepted complete observation nor superseded by a later successful reconciled result.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact required operation and any legitimate superseding evidence; optional diagnostic failures have different significance.

How to fix it

  • Read the entries in completion_feedback.open_requirements (operation_id, status) and inspect each receipt's actual error. Correct the cause, verify current external state, and either produce a later successful result that explicitly supersedes the failed one or have the model report partial or failed accurately; do not replay the mutation while its effect is unknown.
  • Inspect the required operation result and correct or report its unresolved failure.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The required outcome is established or the unresolved result is reported accurately.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
